summary: Verified both HRMS fixes end-to-end. (1) Sliding 30-min inactivity — backend probe (session_inactivity_probe.py) covers fresh login sets last_activity_at; request at 29 min slides forward; background poll /notifications/unread-count does NOT slide; request at 31 min returns 401 with 'Your session expired due to 30 minutes of inactivity. Please log in again.' and session is revoked with revoke_reason=inactivity_timeout; later requests all return 401; POST /auth/refresh on an idle-expired session is rejected and cannot resurrect; refresh alone does not slide; rule applies to admin, employee, intern. Frontend UX verified: after aging localStorage 'blubridge_last_activity' to Date.now()-31*60*1000, watchdog redirects to /login within ~30s, the exact toast is rendered from sessionStorage message, and blubridge_token is cleared. Manual Sign Out works immediately and clears token. (2) Module Visibility — module_visibility_probe.py verifies SELECTED_ONLY, ALL_EXCEPT_SELECTED, OFF and ALL modes with parity across sidebar list, /api/employee/module-visibility, and /api/payslips/my; admin list stays at 13 modules; /api/employee/module-visibility sends Cache-Control: no-store,no-cache,must-revalidate. Frontend UI verified: dinesh.t sidebar renders 12 items with 'My Payslips' and 'Tickets' absent from the DOM (not just CSS-hidden), no flash; admin sidebar unaffected (26 items including Payslips). Original production config was properly restored by the probe: payslips enabled=True, SELECTED_ONLY, selected=['975f8c57-f8ff-4237-af57-07f4a0b1195b'] (Pragathi V Nahar).

minor.issue: Direct URL navigation to /employee/payslips as an unauthorised employee (dinesh.t) does NOT redirect away. The API correctly returns 403 module_unavailable so no payslip data is leaked, but the payslip page shell still renders with the 'No payslips available yet' empty-state text and a 'Failed to load payslips' error toast. Spec asked for an explicit redirect. Add a client-side gate in EmployeeRoute (or in the Payslips page) that checks visibleModules from EmployeeLayout / /api/employee/module-visibility and navigates to /employee/dashboard when the current route's module is not in the visible set. Applies to any other module route as well.

integration_issues.flow: Employee direct URL to a hidden module
integration_issues.issue: Sidebar correctly hides the item, but visiting the route directly still renders the page shell (with a 403 error toast) instead of redirecting to dashboard. No data leak (API returns 403 module_unavailable), only a UX/spec deviation.

action_items: OPTIONAL: add a client-side route guard so navigating directly to an unauthorised module route (e.g. /employee/payslips for dinesh.t) redirects to /employee/dashboard instead of rendering the empty page shell. No data leaks today, but spec asked for a redirect.

Update regression suites for new module-visibility middleware: /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_isolation.py::test_employee_self_service_still_works[/issue-tickets] and [/payslips/my], and /app/backend/tests/test_payslip_auth_layer.py::Test5_EmployeeUnaffected::test_employee_my_payslips_works now fail with 403 module_unavailable because the current production config has tickets=OFF and payslips=SELECTED_ONLY(Pragathi only). These assertions predate the new middleware and must be relaxed (accept 200 or 403 module_unavailable) or the fixture must temporarily flip the module to ALL. Not a code regression — verified via probes and manual API calls; the get_current_user(request, credentials) signature change did NOT break anything.
critical_code_review_comments: Middleware install_module_visibility_guard() is a stateful global gate; ensure it is registered AFTER auth so request.state.current_user is available (already OK). Watch for future endpoints added without an entry in _MODULE_PATH_RULES — they will remain open by default.
EmployeeLayout.js filters the sidebar with fail-CLOSED behaviour on error, which is correct. Consider surfacing a small loading skeleton to avoid a visibly empty menu on slow networks.

AuthContext.js activity clock: the request-interceptor exclusion list (background polls) must be kept in sync with any new polling endpoints added later; suggest centralising the NON_ACTIVITY_PATHS list in one shared constant used by both backend and frontend to prevent drift.

success_rate.backend: 100% (both probes pass; 72/75 legacy regression pass — 3 pre-existing failures caused by production module config, not the new code)
success_rate.frontend: 100% for inactivity + sidebar; 1 minor UX gap on direct URL nav

seed_data_creation: None; module_visibility_probe.py restores original config on exit and it was verified restored (payslips enabled=True, SELECTED_ONLY, selected=Pragathi V Nahar).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both probes are the canonical regression: `python tests/session_inactivity_probe.py <base_url>` and `python tests/module_visibility_probe.py <base_url>`. Both use a Mozilla UA (required to bypass ingress 403). The three 'failing' tests in test_rbac_isolation / test_payslip_auth_layer are known-broken due to the new module_visibility_guard middleware plus current production config (tickets OFF, payslips SELECTED_ONLY to Pragathi) — they need spec-aware fixture updates, they are NOT auth regressions.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in the two features under review. Only one UX gap (no client-side redirect on direct URL) and three legacy regression tests that need updating to reflect the new middleware behaviour.
